title.narrative: Budget Support contract of the EU Support to Entrepreneurship and Private Sector Developmen

description.narrative: Contract related to: Budget Support contract of the EU Support to Entrepreneurship and Private Sector Developmen - The action is fully in line with EU¿s New Agenda for the Mediterranean[1] as it aims at supporting resilient, inclusive, sustainable and connecting economies that create opportunities for all, especially women and youth. It also addresses the priority no. 2 of EU-Jordan Partnership Priorities 2021-2027 by promoting equitable access to employment and employability, in particular of women, young Jordanians and the most vulnerable, and to put in place adequate social safety nets; by creating sustainable jobs, supporting entrepreneurship and innovation. Under the Priority no. 2 of the Multiannual Indicative Programme (MIP) 2021-2027, this action confirms the EU will provide support to the improvement of Jordan¿s business climate, access to finance and financial inclusion, including for women, support entrepreneurship and promote investments in sectors that have the greatest potential to generate sustainable employment, in an effort to help Jordan diversify its economy and attract Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs). In this respect, the action could support the recently launched EU-Jordan investment platform, a crucial milestone for the implementation of EU¿s Economic and Investment Plan. The platform discusses public investments, including the upgrade of the King Hussein/Allenby Bridge. This action is aligned with the Government of Jordan¿s Indicative Executive Program (GIEP) 2021-2024 that reaffirms the commitment to policies and reforms focused on enabling an investment climate and business environment, enhancing competition and increasing employment, and supporting key sectors.  This action aims to stimulate sustainable and inclusive employment through entrepreneurship and private sector development in Jordan, by means of enhancing the business environment, capacitating the different stakeholders of the entrepreneurship ecosystem and promoting inclusive and decent job opportunities. Consequently, the programme is expected to impact the socio-economic well-being and self-reliance of Jordanians and, potentially, Syrian refugees. This programme aims at piloting the humanitarian-development nexus in the fields of livelihoods, social protection and economic growth.The action proposes interventions to increase private sector employment opportunities, focusing on the implementation, monitoring and evaluation of a relevant and credible policy on entrepreneurship interlinked with other relevant strategies; strengthening stakeholders¿ capacities for employability (both demand and supply) and promotion of an entrepreneurship ecosystem in the country.  The proposed action complements and builds synergies with the parallel Special Measure EU Support to Livelihoods under the regional response to the Syrian crisis. The linkages are made through concrete activities under SO1 and SO2 which expand the target beneficiaries to include vulnerable Jordanians and Syrian refugees. The action will also linked with the Partnership Implementation Facility (¿Sharaka¿) which will provide support to the Jordanian administration in developing regulatory and policy frameworks that are conducive for green, digital and inclusive growth. Finally, the action will also closely coordinate with the ongoing EU Support to Economic Reforms for Growth and Jobs programme.

title.narrative: Increase in the national exports through the implementation of the national export strategy (20232025).

description.narrative: The National Export Strategy for the years (20232025) and its Executive Plan for the National Export Strategy are expected to be approved by the end of the first quarter of 2023. Following an internal indepth study for national export study, the strategy foresees an ambitious target of 5% annual growth yearonyear. The relevant Ministry has almost finalised (by end of first quarter of 2023) the strategys action plan with more than 100 activities covering the main pillars: enhancing the competitiveness, the quality of exports, diversify the product basket of goods & services and enhance access to nontraditional markets. The Ministry is also currently working on very detailed Tracking Tools containing live dashboard to follow up the implementations of each activity. The strategy was launched in March 2023. The value of national (local) exports is increased by 15% from the baseline year (2022) as reported in Jordans Department of Statistics (DoS),

title.narrative: Number of Startups business performance enhanced

description.narrative: 25 startups supported with business development services show improvement in business performance through one or the other below criterion: Increase in the number of employees by 50%: the number of employees is shown in the documentation provided to Social the Security Corporation (SCC) on monthly basis, so to calculate the percentage of increase in the number of employees the following equation is applied: (Number of employees for year 2025 Number of employees for year 2024) / Number of employees for year 2024 Increase in revenue by 50%: the total increase in revenue is shown in company annual financial reports, to calculate the percentage: (increase in revenue of year 2025 increase in revenue of year 2024) / increase in revenue of year 2024

comment.narrative: 25 startups supported with business development services show business performance

title.narrative: Number of new feasible ideas incubated for the preseed stage

description.narrative: Leapfrogging means that a business project will take less time from ideation into seed stage with the help of business sector, technical people and academia. The ideation hub will be an eplatform that will link all universities, vocational centres, business sector, and intermediaries with startups. from the 400 screened and selected ideas through the innovation, 100 ideas in the fields of ICT and ICT enabled businesses, handicraft, energy, manufacturing, agriculture and gaming are incubated for the preseed stage. The project is considering collecting the best 400 ideas from industry, universities and startups using the hub and starting the preseed stage of 25% of them. In a survey of 2021 which included 9 of the ecosystem participants (accelerators, incubators) it was found that 410 ideas got out of the screening process they conduct and an average of 11.5% of these were selected for investment.

comment.narrative: 100 of 400 ideas or 25 are incubated by the ecosystem for the preseed stage.

title.narrative: Number of SMEs obtaining an international certificate

description.narrative: This indicator is directly extracted from JEDCOs Strategy 20222025, which aims at supporting Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to enhance their productivity, marketing & raise competitiveness locally and internationally. The strategic objective behind this indicator is to support SMEs reach convenient environment & international standards. The strategy builds on the Vision 2025 and the Economic Modernisation Visions objective to strengthen Jordans international competitiveness. From the total number of SMEs supported, at least 17 obtain an international accreditation demonstrated by a valid certificate.

comment.narrative: 70 17 of SMEs supported obtaining international accreditation
